cross_family_review.first_review_followup: Isolated inherited Git environment and prevented upward repository discovery; both protections were tested by mutation.
limitations: This is a static review of the provided module and materializer context. I did not execute the tests or the mutation runs, and I did not verify the reported validation results or source hash.

Snapshot mode is chosen when ROOT/.git is absent. That is sound here only because the trusted materializer rejects any path component that casefolds to '.git', so a snapshot never contains one. A different materializer would need separate review.

_disk_files does not follow symlinks below the prefix. os.scandir on the prefix itself does follow a symlinked 'evaluation' or 'evaluation/banks' component. The materializer rejects symlinks in snapshots, and in checkouts the index listing still reports the symlink entry. Only names are enumerated either way, never contents.

Matching of the 'sealed' component is case-sensitive, and only paths under evaluation/banks are scanned. Variants such as 'Sealed/' on case-insensitive filesystems, or sealed material stored elsewhere in the repository, are outside this guard's scope as specified.

_git removes every GIT_* variable, including GIT_CONFIG_COUNT and GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS. If a CI runner relied on those to set options such as safe.directory, git ls-files would raise loudly rather than pass silently. That is acceptable under the fail-closed requirement, but it was not checked against the actual CI configuration.
The fixture tests need a git binary and symlink support. They may error rather than skip on platforms without symlinks, such as Windows without developer mode.
No sealed bank contents were read or requested. This review does not assess the product quality of the banks or of the evaluation.

measurement_limits: Synthetic fixtures only; no heldout bank contents were read.
Guard is scoped to exact sealed path components under evaluation/banks.
Snapshot scanning relies on the trusted materializer rejecting aliases and symlinks.
Cross-family code review is advisory; no model-judge qualification or product-quality certificate is inferred.
